properties.title: Orthopyroxene Abundance · Kaguya SP South Polar 50-90S (Lemelin et al. 2022)
properties.authors: Myriam Lemelin, Paul G. Lucey, Alex Camon
properties.crs: Source: Moon_2000_Stereographic_South_Pole (1737400 m sphere, true scale at the pole), georeferenced only by corner GCPs in the .aux.xml sidecar, rows stored bottom-up. COG: IAU:30135, north-up, same grid.
properties.processing:lineage: Kaguya Spectral Profiler reflectance, gridded, interpolated and scaled to LRO LOLA 1064 nm reflectance; mineral abundance modeled as described in Lemelin et al. (2022), section 3.4. Distributed on Zenodo as a Float32 GeoTIFF in weight fraction with Esri sidecars. COG: gdal_translate assigns IAU:30135 and the bottom-up geotransform given by the GCP corners (+/-1267472 m); gdal_calc.py multiplies values by 100 to wt%; gdalwarp with nearest neighbor onto the identical extent and size flips rows to north-up with pixel values unchanged, and writes a COG with DEFLATE/PREDICTOR=3 compression.
properties.lri:data_use_note: Orthopyroxene abundance at 1 km/pixel for the south polar region (50-90S). Low-calcium pyroxene is characteristic of noritic crustal lithologies.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: Spectral Profiler mineral model at 1 km/pixel, 50-90S. No NoData value; pixels outside the mapped circle are 0 in all four mineral maps.
properties.lri:quality_note: The raster has no NoData value. Inside the mapped circle (data reach 49.9 deg latitude) the four SP mineral maps sum to exactly 100 wt% at every pixel, so 0 is a zero abundance there; 0.2% of pixels poleward of 50 deg are 0 in this map. Outside the circle all four maps are 0 as fill. Source values are weight fraction (maximum 0.744); the COG stores wt%. Source rows are stored bottom-up and georeferenced only by GCPs; the COG is north-up. Along the 49.9-50 deg boundary ring the mean is 25.5 wt% here and 13.6 wt% in the Kaguya MI 50N-50S map (correlation 0.65), so the two products do not join seamlessly. Lemelin et al. (2022) name this mineral low-calcium pyroxene; it is grouped with the MI orthopyroxene map.
